A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EELMA and retain identifiable corresponding methods, experiments, and appendices. The complete text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison despite substantial rewriting, reformatting, and added appendices in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gridworld, Tower of Hanoi, and WebArena experiments, including empowerment estimates, task performance, authentication results, and appendix comparisons with natural-language conversion and a prompt-only estimator.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds tau-bench evaluations, trajectory-metric comparisons, WebArena error analysis, and encoder and fine-tuning experiments.

M1.justification: The paired InfoNCE objectives and difference-of-scores estimator remain. v3 introduces LoRA encoder adaptation and recommends it as the default; Appendix D also changes the reported WebArena embedding model from Jina embeddings to E5-Mistral-7B and adds an encoder layer. These are bounded architectural adaptations within the retained estimation procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds tau-bench airline and retail customer-service tasks using structured function-calling tools, extending evaluation beyond textual games and web browsing (Section 5, Figure 8). Gridworld, Tower of Hanoi, the four WebArena domains, natural-language conversion, and the authentication scenario were already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: New Appendix C.3 and Table 5 compare EELMA with five trajectory-derived alternatives: discounted visitation entropy, action entropy, normalized state coverage, trajectory length, and unique-state ratio. This substantially expands comparisons of the proposed capability metric. Direct estimation and the Gemini-2.5-Flash prompt-only estimator already appeared in v1 and remain.

E3.justification: v3 adds tau-bench evaluation on 50 airline and 115 retail tasks with three Qwen2.5 scales, and adds Qwen2.5-32B-it to WebArena. New baseline correlations pool 16 WebArena and six tau-bench model-domain points. Authentication reporting introduces within-trajectory averaging. Appendix B.2 revises the stated training schedule from approximately 10,000 steps to a 20,000-step maximum while retaining convergence near 10,000; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices K–L newly test sensitivity to three embedding models and four encoder-training strategies, examining accuracy, training collapse, and computational costs. Appendix G.2 adds analysis of off-domain WebArena navigation. These substantially extend v1's existing complexity, CoT, memory, linguistic-variation, and authentication analyses.

E5.justification: Authentication reporting now distinguishes trajectory-level averages from pooled action-level statistics and explicitly displays numerical ± uncertainties in Figure 9, although their type is unspecified. The action-level standard deviations and Welch tests remain in Figure 11. Three-seed WebArena reporting and five-replicate prompt-estimator comparisons are retained; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: v3 adds Qwen WebArena outcomes, positive airline and inverted retail empowerment trends, and Table 5's baseline correlations, including EELMA values of 0.39 for WebArena and 0.71 for tau-bench. Tables 7–8 add encoder accuracy and training-collapse results. Authentication means change from 0.365/-0.127 in v1 Figure 8 to trajectory-level 0.268/-0.094 in v3 Figure 9; the original action-level values remain in v3 Figure 11, so this is reaggregation rather than a performance change.

T1.justification: Section 3 revises the formal empowerment averaging and normalization, replacing gamma^t/(1-gamma) with geometric weights (1-gamma)gamma^k. It also replaces the asserted exact score-difference estimate with an approximation requiring a small expected residual difference and explicitly discusses finite-negative-sample bias. These materially revise the core mathematical definition and justification, while Appendix A's reward-bound lemmas and proofs largely persist.

C1.justification: The central contributions—text-based empowerment estimation, a goal-agnostic capability proxy, and identification of influential actions—remain. v3 extends its expressly claimed applicability to realistic tool use and emphasizes a complementary role alongside task-success measures in the abstract and conclusion, modestly revising the scope and qualification of the claims.

C2.justification: v3 substantially clarifies failure conditions: task-irrelevant control during off-domain navigation, misleading diversity near floor performance in retail, and finite-sample estimator bias. Appendix I also replaces v1's broad robustness interpretation with explicit acknowledgment of substantial Hanoi degradation using retained results. New architectural analyses motivate LoRA and qualify unrestricted fine-tuning, materially improving the discussion of applicability.

D1.justification: v1 already provides pseudocode, prompts, optimizer settings, dimensions, and hardware information. v3 adds LoRA rank 8 and alpha 16, specifies partial tuning of the final two layers, and reports H100 memory overheads. It updates the advertised code location from an anonymous host to a named GitHub repository and corrects Gridworld and WebArena setup descriptions.

R1.justification: v3 adds targeted references for LoRA, tau-bench, E5-Mistral, online learning, and related empowerment training. Appendix M distinguishes semantic state-level empowerment from Ellis et al.'s token-level approach. The central positioning relative to empowerment and benchmark-based evaluation remains; publication-year and venue updates to retained references are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanation, and discussion are extensively rewritten. v3 separates the capability hypothesis more clearly, explains latent states versus observations, reorganizes contributions and appendix headings, moves existing multimodal and power-seeking discussion into Appendix M, and adds an Impact Statement. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout, with widespread resizing and relocation of figures and tables. v3 redraws the method overview and several plots, expands Figure 7 with Qwen, and revises the authentication display. New tool-use, off-domain navigation, encoder, and fine-tuning figures and comparison tables substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important validation gaps through comparisons with simpler metrics, evaluation in tool-use environments, and controlled encoder analyses. It also corrects overly broad interpretations of linguistic robustness and makes estimator bias and capability-proxy failures explicit. These substantially strengthen the evidence and clarify its limits. Reporting problems remain, including stale WebArena correlations in the prose and Figure 12's mismatch between state-level plots and trajectory-level captions, but they do not outweigh the stronger comparisons and more qualified conclusions.
